Resolves #19780

`AnimatedRowSorting.spec.mjs` now waits for the AnimateRows plugin before it sorts or filters, so a cold load can no longer turn its animation tests red.

The grid body imports the plugin on demand, and the rows can render before the plugin and its stylesheet are in place. `openExample()` waited only for the rows. On #19776's merge run, the filter therefore ran through the body's own handler, and Carol jumped from 128 to 64 with no frame in between (e2e-engine 1/3, run 38799316487).

- `openExample()` waits for the body's `neo-animate-rows` class, which reaches the DOM only together with the plugin's stylesheet.
- A route handler holds `AnimateRows.mjs` until the rows show, then 500 ms more, so every run puts the rows first, as a cold load can, and the wait is always exercised.
- Test-only: the plugin and the example are unchanged.

Related: #19774 (the spec) · #19776 (the failed run) · #6858

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium, real App Worker, the e2e engine tier) → L3 required (the defect is the order in which a real page loads the plugin and renders the rows).

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the Shared PR Baseline jobs run in CI.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `openExample()` ends with `expect(page.locator('.neo-grid-body.neo-animate-rows')).toHaveCount(1)`, before any test sorts or filters. |
| AC-2 | The route handler holds the plugin module in every run. Without AC-1's wait, the sort and filter tests fail 6/6 over 3 repeats with the CI sequence (`128, 128, 128, 64, …` and `160, …, 0`). With it, they pass. |
| AC-3 | `--repeat-each=10` → 30/30; e2e engine tier 274 passed, 3 skipped. |
